116	
117	Writes outside the repository **fail** rather than appearing to work. `$HOME` is
118	read-only, the same for both tool users, and package-manager caches are redirected
119	to a writable directory by the runner. An error an agent can read beats a success
120	it cannot trust.
121	
122	### Which credentials a tool server can reach
123	
124	A credential reaches the Atoma process and the servers that name it. Nothing else
125	— not a later workflow step, and not a server in the other class. The classes
126	differ in what the limit means inside them.
127	
128	**A credential declared for a shipped server** is on `atomaton-tools`. The shell
129	and third-party servers cannot read it. Another shipped server can reach it only
130	by a deliberate attempt, which is what the servers' own hardening and the PATH
131	narrowing are for.
132	
133	**A credential declared for a third-party server** is on `atomaton-untrusted`.
134	Treat it as reachable by the shell and by every other third-party server. That is
135	the cost of running a program whose implementation cannot be changed.
136	
137	**None of this stops intent, only accident.** An agent reads issue text written by
138	anyone who can open an issue, and a prompt injection can ask it to do whatever a
139	tool allows. What remains is the controls that always mattered: declare only the
140	credentials a tool genuinely needs, and read the diff when a governed file
141	changes.
142	
143	Which of your secrets a run is handed is settled before any of this, by
144	[the ref a declaration is read from](../pipeline/how-it-works.md). Four things
145	fail the run rather than being quietly dropped, and a fifth is only a warning;
146	[`tools.secrets`](reference.md#toolssecrets) lists them.
147	
148	### What a shell command may print
149	
150	A shell command's output is redacted before the agent, the run log, the session,
151	or an issue comment ever sees it. Two things are removed: text shaped like a
152	vendor credential (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `AKIA`, a PEM header, and similar), and the
153	exact values of the API key and tokens the run itself holds.
154	
155	This is a net, not a control. A value *derived* from a secret — a slice of a key,
156	a base64 of one — is indistinguishable from ordinary text and gets through. Keep
157	secrets your agents do not need out of their environment, and treat this as the
158	thing that catches the accident rather than the thing that makes it safe.
159	
160	It exists because two of the three places a run's output lands are otherwise
161	unprotected: GitHub Actions substitutes `***` for registered secrets in the
162	workflow log, and does nothing for the issue comment a run posts or for the
163	session JSON on the `atomaton-data` branch.
164	
165	**How much it may print** is a separate limit, and it is not configurable. A long
166	stdout or stderr keeps its beginning and its **end**, with a marker naming how
167	much went from the middle and `output_truncated` set on the result. Both ends,
168	because command output is both kinds of text at once: a header or a command echo
169	worth seeing, and a failure at the bottom.
170	
171	That end used to be the part that was dropped — the cap was a million bytes and it
172	kept the head, so a build log that overran returned its banner rather than its
173	error. A million bytes is also about 250k tokens, more than a context window, from
174	one call. See [writing a tool](tasks/write-a-tool.md) for why that matters beyond
175	the one run, and [what a record does not keep](../records/boundaries.md) for the
176	second cap the same text meets on its way into a session.
177	
178	## Why the agent's own run is Linux
179	
180	`runs_on` sets the machine for the jobs that run **your** commands. It does not
181	reach the agent's own run, which stays on Linux, because what isolates a tool
182	server from the others is Linux-only top to bottom: `useradd` for the two users
183	with no sudo, one sudoers rule for the downward drop, `setfacl` for the ACLs,
184	`prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE)`, `/proc/<pid>/environ` being the thing closed. Making that
185	configurable would mean an agent's shell running with every one of those
186	protections silently absent.
187	
188	## The three facts the arrangement rests on
189	
190	Each was measured on the runner rather than reasoned about, and each is why one of
191	the alternatives was not taken. They are stated here because the design depends on
192	them and nothing else says so.
193	
194	**`PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0)` does not survive `execve`.** A process can make its own
195	`/proc/<pid>/environ` unreadable to the same user, but the flag is cleared when it
196	execs something else. So nothing can set it on another program's behalf — the
197	program has to call it in its own process. That is why the servers this project
198	ships call it themselves, and why a third-party server cannot be made to.
199	
200	**`LD_PRELOAD` would have closed both holes and does not work here.** A shared
201	library's constructor runs after `exec`, inside the new process, so the flag would
202	stick — and `LD_PRELOAD` is itself an environment variable, so every descendant
203	would inherit it. It fails on `gh`, which is written in Go and statically linked: a
204	static binary ignores `LD_PRELOAD` entirely. The `github` server runs `gh` with
205	`GH_TOKEN` in its environment, so the child-process hole would have stayed open.
206	
207	**A different uid closes the environ hole outright.** That is the mechanism taken,
208	and it is why there are two users rather than a container: the container answered
209	the same question with `--user 1234:0`, which is the same problem without the
210	container.

## 何に効き、何が優先するか

このrunが**人に向けて書く日本語**すべてが対象になる — 報告コメント、質問、相談、プルリクエストの本文、サブIssueの本文、次の担当への引き継ぎ。

対象外は、コード、コミットメッセージ、機構が固定で持っている英文、報告契約そのものの見出し語。

**報告の契約が優先する。** システムプロンプトの報告は四つの部からなり、そのうち三つに上限がある。残る「確かめられなかったこと」には上限がなく、切り詰めてはいけない。このスキルはその枠の中で文を整えるだけで、枠を変えない。衝突したら契約に従う。

**投稿する前に、一度だけ読み直す。** 下書きをこの原則で通し、直してから出す。報告はrunの最後に一度しか書かれないので、読み直しの機会はここしかない。

以下は [yomiyasu](https://github.com/nanaism/yomiyasu) v2.5.0（MIT）の変換原則を、推敲ではなく**生成向け**に組み直したもの。上流は追わない。

## 一文

**主語と述語を離さない。** 一読で「誰が何をしたか」が追えること。修飾を主述の間に長く挟むと、読み手は述語を探して戻る。挟むなら文を分ける。

> ✗ この変更は、前回の議論で保留にされていた点を踏まえたうえで、今回の判断として取り込むことにしました。
> ○ 前回はこの点を保留にしていました。今回は取り込みます。

**指示語の先を確定させる。** 「これ」「その方針」「前者」は、直前の一文だけを読んで指す先が決まる位置に置く。決まらないなら名詞に戻す。

**長さの目安は一文30〜45字、読点は0〜2個。** 超えたら、読点を足すのではなく文を割る。間を作るためだけの読点は外す。並んだ語句を区切る読点、外すと係り先が変わる読点は残す。

## 文末

**終わったことを「〜します」と書かない。** 報告で最も多い病。直したなら「修正しました」、いま直しているなら「修正しています」、これからなら「修正します」。この三つを文末で書き分ける。

**言い切りの強さを変えない。** 確かめたことは「〜です」、推測は「〜と考えられます」。弱めるのは事実でないときだけ。

**文末を散らすこと自体を目的にしない。** 同じ文末が続いて単調なら、語順と文のまとめ方で整える。文の働き（説明・依頼・報告）は変えない。
